title: Spin-up batch release playlist and KPI handoff
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is a lightweight operational tracker + KPI handoff for small-batch feature releases (10-50k users/day). It mixes a sprint-friendly checklist with a compact KPI matrix so Product Ops + SRE can run canaries and hand off monitoring to oncall quickly.

How to use: (TL;DR)
- Maintain one row per feature-batch (cohort).
- Fill ownership, SLOs, guardrails and primary dashboards before canary.
- Use the decision column to record go/no-go at 15/50/100% traffic.
- Post-launch: record immediate quality regressions and assign to triage owners.

Column definitions (sheet layout):
- Batch ID: short id, e.g. BATCH-2026-03-A
- Feature short name: e.g. "assistant-safety-tweak"
- Owner: product lead (name + slack handle)
- Eng lead: (name)
- SRE lead: (name)
- Canary plan: canary % & duration (e.g. 5% for 2h, 20% for 4h)
- Primary KPI (metric): e.g. latency_p50_ms, token_cost_per_call, success_rate
- Baseline (pre-release): numeric baseline value + source dashboard id
- Target / Acceptable delta: e.g. latency +10% allowed, error_rate <0.5ppt
- Rollback triggers: explicit thresholds (e.g. p95 latency > 600ms for 10m OR error_rate > 1.5x baseline for 5m)
- Observability hooks: list of dashboards/events (Links)
- Canary verdict: pass | fail | degraded + notes
- Traffic step history: text log of percent/time stamps (quick copy/paste)
- Post-launch regression notes: free text
- Postmortem owner + ETA: who will own analysis
- Release tags: prod/dedicated/private (where deployed)
- Compliance notes: if customer-sensitive (Y/N)

Compact KPI Library (examples to copy into "Primary KPI"):
- lat_p50_ms, lat_p95_ms, p99_latency_ms
- token_cost_per_call_usd, avg_tokens_per_call
- success_rate_pct (successful responses without error)
- hallucination_signal_rate (eval harness flag)
- infra_util_gpu_pct, queue_time_ms
- api_4xx_rate, api_5xx_rate

Decision heuristics (quick reference):
- Canary PASS: no rollback triggers during canary and primary KPI within target. Move to next step after full confirmation period.
- Canary FLAG: KPI degraded but below rollback threshold and degradation has clear mitigations; pause and observe with SRE.
- Canary FAIL: immediate rollback. Trigger oncall + product hotfix lane.

Preflight checklist (must be green before canary):
- [ ] Feature flags in place and tested locally (FF: batch-<id>)
- [ ] Load tests ran for expected throughput (attach brief)
- [ ] Autoscaling policy validated by infra (commit id or PR)
- [ ] Observability: dashboards created and pinned; alerts created (alert ids)
- [ ] Runbook stub created: brief steps for rollback and rollback validation
- [ ] Legal / compliance signoff (if required)
- [ ] Customer impact list reviewed (internal customers, pilot users)

Owner handoff notes (what SRE needs at is-give):
- Primary KPI and baseline (one-line)
- Expected traffic profile and payload size distribution
- KV cache effects and warmup expectations
- Any model quantization or new model version details
- Short list of likely failure modes and mitigations already considered

Contingency playbook (short):
- Trigger: Rollback conditions met -> steps:
  1) Toggle FF to previous state (owner: Eng lead)
  2) Apply emergency routing fallback to stable model variant (SRE runbook step)
  3) Notify customers on the customer-impact list + CSM (if > 1% user base)
  4) Create triage ticket (JIRA) and assign to oncall rotational owner

Monitoring handoff (after reaching 100% and stability window closed):
- Product-ops to add the batch row into weekly KPI digest (owner)
- Oncall to include regressions in daily incident digest for 72h post-launch
- Product to schedule qualitative evaluation (prompt sets / user examples) within 7 days

Post-launch questions to capture (for the postmortem):
- Was latency change transient or sustained?
- Which downstream services showed correlated change?
- Any user segments disproportionately affected? (region, plan, router)
- Anything surprising in token usage per call?

Notes-to-self / open items (working list):
- Need a smaller "hallucination smoke" script amenable to run during canary (Sofia to prototype)
- Consider adding an "economic delta" column (est delta per 100k calls)
- Reconcile with Launch Control master (Confluence) weekly; this sheet is lightweight, not canonical for SLAs

Quick template row (copy-paste):
- BATCH-2026-03-A | assistant-safety-tweak | Maya T (@mayat) | Owen P | Rakesh I | 5% 2h -> 20% 4h -> 100% 12h | success_rate_pct | baseline 99.6% (dash: SRE/dash/231) | target >= 99.4% | rollback: error_rate >1.5x baseline for 10m or p95 > 800ms for 5m | dash links: https://dash/231, https://logs/feature/231 | verdict: pending | traffic log: 5% 2026-03-11T14:00 -> 20% 2026-03-11T16:30 | post-launch: --- | postmortem owner: Maya T (ETA 2026-03-18) | tags: hosted-api | compliance: N

Communication plan (short):
- Pre-canary: Slack #launch-control post with one-line summary + link to sheet (owner: Product-ops)
- Canary transitions: ephemeral updates in the same thread (SRE lead)
- Rollback + incident: use #ops-incident channel and escalate to EM if rollback triggered
- Postmortem: publish within 5 business days to Confluence and link in sheet

Why this differs from the master playbook:
- Designed for speed: compact KPI + clear rollback triggers to enable 1-2 person quick launches
- Emphasizes a short handoff for monitoring so oncall can absorb new batches during noisy weeks
- Lightweight postmortem cadence to keep cadence high without huge admin burden

Revision history (notes):
- 2025-11-03 created initial template (Maya T)
- 2026-01-12 added compact KPI library and decision heuristics (Sofia A)
- 2026-03-10 updated rollback thresholds after DB latency incident (Owen P)

TODOs (next short list):
- [ ] Add economic delta column (Maya)
- [ ] Prototype hallucination smoke checks (Sofia)
- [ ] Link common dashboards as template variables (Rakesh)

End of sheet.
